title: Model By-Laws for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)
content:
A Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) is the village-level cooperative institution and the foundation of the short-term cooperative credit structure in India, operating under state Cooperative Societies Acts and its own registered by-laws.

Membership: Any individual who is a resident of the area of operation, is of sound mind, has attained 18 years of age, and agrees to abide by the by-laws may apply for membership. Membership is granted by the managing committee on payment of the prescribed admission fee and purchase of at least one share. A member may withdraw from the society by giving notice in writing, subject to the society's liquidity position.

Services a member is entitled to: short-term and medium-term agricultural credit (crop loans), input supply (seeds, fertilizers), storage facilities where available, and since the 2023 Ministry of Cooperation initiative, access to Common Service Centre (CSC) services such as banking correspondent services, Aadhaar-linked services, insurance, and utility bill payments at many computerised PACS.

Managing committee: Elected by the general body for a term as prescribed in the by-laws (typically 5 years), responsible for sanctioning loans, maintaining accounts, and conducting the society's day-to-day business within limits set by the general body.

Loan procedure: A member applies in the prescribed form, the managing committee scrutinises the application against the individual's cropping pattern and repaying capacity (often linked to the Kisan Credit Card scheme), and disburses the sanctioned amount, usually before the start of the cropping season. Loans carry interest as fixed by the society, subject to any government interest-subvention scheme in force.

Default and recovery: If a loan is not repaid by the due date, the society may charge penal interest as specified in the by-laws and pursue recovery under the state Cooperative Societies Act's recovery provisions, which allow recovery as arrears of land revenue in many states — but only after due process and notice to the member.

Grievance route: A member dissatisfied with a decision of the managing committee (loan refusal, membership issue, etc.) may first appeal to the general body at its next meeting, and if unresolved, approach the Assistant/District Registrar of Cooperative Societies, who has powers to inquire into and adjudicate disputes involving PACS under the state Act.
